newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates flat as oil loads at al-Bakr.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates flat as oil loads at al-Bakr.

text.p: Crude oil tanker chartering rates for Mideast/Japan routes were little changed on Monday as the first tankers in five years loaded from the Iraqi port of Mina al-Bakr, shipbrokers said.

Bayoil fixed the 265,000 tonne Leonidas from Mina al-Bakr to the U.S. Gulf at W50, while Coastal fixed the 260,000 tonne Star Africa to Aruba. The rate was not reported, but one broker thought it was a couple of points below W50.
"These are quite old ships and they have not been too discerning," one broker said.
At least two brokers said they had heard of a 20,000 barrel oil spillage off South Korea over the weekend but these reports could not be confirmed immediately.
North Sea markets were steady. SPI fixed the 75,000 tonne Olympic Sponsor at W136 to the USAC, but brokers said enquiry for larger tonnage sailing transatlantic was very limited.

Transatlantic rates for 130,000 tonners were notionally pegged at around W97.5 while those for the 250,000 tonne vessels were closer to W62.5. "But there is no talk in these markets so it is hard to assess," one dealer said.
Rates for 130,000 tonne Suezmaxes and 80,000 tonne Aframaxes making cross-Med voyages were little changed at W87.5 and W107.5 respectively.
While the 120,000 tonne Ninemea was fixed for a cross-Med voyage at as sickly W76, brokers said this was well below the market because of the age of the ship.

They said fuel oil tanker fixing for 25,000 tonners moving in the U.K.-Cont and the Med were fairly quiet, with W190 seen close to the market level for both. A 50,000 tonne fuel vessel, the Louros, was seen going transatlantic at about W150-W155.
